findings.observation: A publicly indexed RTEC instruction page publishes two kiosk-exit password values in plaintext.
actions: Rotate/revoke the exposed kiosk credentials immediately if they remain valid.
Remove/redact credentials from the public page and any linked image/document.
Purge or request recrawl/removal of cached/search-indexed copies where practical.
Audit affected kiosk/device fleet for unauthorized kiosk exits or configuration changes.
Move device-admin secrets into managed configuration/MDM or another authenticated channel rather than static public instructions.
Search the public site and attached documents for other password/PIN/token exposures.

findings.observation: Current public instructions tell prospective riders to provide sensitive identifiers such as Medicaid and/or Social Security information to a CSR for profile/trip setup.
actions: Document approved collection channel, minimum necessary fields, verification method, retention location, access roles and redaction/logging rules.
Ensure agents/knowledge systems never copy these identifiers into durable general memory.
Validate whether both identifiers are actually required in every intake case.

findings.observation: Current public instructions allow riders to provide debit/credit-card information by phone as one EPG loading method.
actions: Document approved payment-card handling process and ensure card data is not written into ordinary email, notes, logs or agent memory.
Prefer provider-hosted payment flows where operationally appropriate.
Validate staff training and access boundaries for telephone card handling.

security_boundary: Do not store the exposed credential values in GitHub, Agent OS memory, logs or user-facing analysis.
A public secret remains a secret and should be treated as compromised rather than normalized as public knowledge.
Sensitive rider identifiers/payment data are operational inputs, not reusable profile knowledge.
